text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions and its affiliate, the Zimbabwe Electricity and Energy Workers' Union, have strongly criticised President Robert Mugabe's government for signing a deal with a Malaysian company YTL Corp Bhd to privatise Hwange Thermal Power Station.

YTL will control 51 percent of the station under the multi-million dollar deal which has met fierce opposition in the southern African state over allegations it was not transparent and should have gone through the tender board. The government denies the deal was shady but a private placement, and this week it sacked the entire board of the Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA) over the dispute.

- A leading Zimbabwean tobacco trader and private property developer plans to build a Z$20 million tobacco auction floor covering 8,000 square metres in Zimbabwe's northwestern town of Chinhoyi -- the fourth for the country -- and hopes to have it running by 1998. Zimbabwe is the world's third largest producer of flu-cured tobacco.

- Zimbabwe's annual programme of providing basic free seed and fertiliser packs to poor peasants will cost it Z$212 million this year, up from Z$180 million spent on the programme last year, the permanent secretary in the ministry of agriculture, Tobias Takavarasha, told the Herald.
Takavarasha said about 1.2 million peasant families normally benefit from the programme aimed at boosting food production.
